status_summary: The HUD Secretary announced a HUD task force under the Department of Government Efficiency effort in mid-February 2025, described as made up of HUD employees reviewing spending; political-appointee composition and an ideology mandate are not stated. On 2025-02-20 the Secretary announced cancellation of about $4 million in diversity-related contracts. HUD terminated 78 Fair Housing Initiatives Program grants on 2025-02-27; a federal court in Massachusetts issued a temporary restraining order on 2025-03-26, dissolved it on 2025-04-14 citing a Supreme Court stay that pointed such claims to the Court of Federal Claims, and the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case on 2025-12-22. HUD also withdrew fair housing guidance through a 2025-09-17 memo, formalized in notices published 2026-04-06 (eight documents) and 2026-07-17 (13 Office of General Counsel documents).

timeline.event: The HUD Secretary announced cancellation of about $4 million in diversity-related contracts after launching a DOGE task force.

HUD published the interim final rule Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing Revisions (90 FR 11020, effective 2025-04-02), repealing the 2021 AFFH interim final rule, one of the prior-administration actions the text targets.
A federal district court in Massachusetts issued a 14-day temporary restraining order requiring HUD to reinstate terminated Fair Housing Initiatives Program grants for the plaintiffs.
The court dissolved the temporary restraining order, citing the Supreme Court stay in Department of Education v. California and Court of Federal Claims jurisdiction.
HUD issued a memo withdrawing nine fair housing guidance documents dated 2007 to 2024.
The plaintiffs filed a stipulation of voluntary dismissal without prejudice, closing the district court case.
HUD published a notice (91 FR 17291) withdrawing eight fair housing guidance documents, effective 2025-09-17.
HUD published a notice (91 FR 44867) withdrawing 13 Office of General Counsel guidance documents, effective 2025-09-25.

title: Create a HUD task force to reverse Biden-era progressive-ideology actions
uncertainties: The task force's charter and membership were not found in any primary HUD document; the HUD task force reported by news outlets in February 2025 was set up under the government efficiency order to review spending, its members are not named, and it is not described as limited to political appointees or as charged with reversing ideology-based actions. The stage therefore rests on operative reversals by other instruments; several of those reversals (AFFH, PAVE, climate initiatives, guidance withdrawals) are tracked as their own records (c15-01, c15-05, c15-06, c15-10), so this record overlaps them. The AFFH interim final rule event is copied from the verified sibling record c15-01. Both guidance withdrawal notices (2026-04-06 and 2026-07-17) were read in full on federalregister.gov in review; neither mentions a task force. A Federal Register API query of HUD documents since 2026-04-01, run in review on 2026-10-18, found no guidance withdrawal notice after 2026-07-17. The temporary restraining order date (2025-03-26) and the 2025-12-22 dismissal come from a docket summary on clearinghouse.net; the court docket itself could not be opened. The 2025-09-17 memo and the 2026-04-06 notice cover largely the same documents.
